tasks.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H32): New design: library-lean four-launch pipeline (LN in K1 via cluster DSMEM stats, cuBLASLt GELU epilogue, one-launch GRN scale, swap-AB NCHW GEMM2 with residual, L2 weight prefetch). Build from scratch (you may read the r0 baseline r0-convnext-coop-fp32-anchor for host plumbing and the per-lineage conclusions for recipes; no other lineage code). Target rows in order: the six wide-C rows (2,768; 8,768; 16,768; 32,768; 8,384; 16,384), then the HW=784 rows (1,192; 4,192; 8,192), then 1,160,449,7, then 1,96 / 2,96 if time allows. Rows you do not reach run a simple correct fallback (the r0 baseline path is acceptable); the merge keeps A there. CUDA C++ two-file layout (kernel.cu without torch headers, binding.cpp), cuBLASLt from the binding, one handle and per-shape plans set up on first use and valid in any shape order. STEP 0, kill gates, cold after a 2xL2 zero-fill, harness_time x3, interleave the r0 anchor: (a) cuBLASLt fp16 GEMM1 [M x C]x[C x 4C] with CUBLASLT_EPILOGUE_GELU_BIAS (fp16 out, fp32 compute) vs EPILOGUE_BIAS at 392x3072x768, 1568x1536x384, 784x768x192: the GELU delta must be <= 1.5 us per shape (kill at > 3 us on two shapes). (b) GEMM2 in the swap-AB batched form: per image b, D_b[C x HW] = W2[C x 4C] * h_b^T (h_b fp16 [HW x 4C] row-major, so op(B) = T), beta = 1 with C_b = x_b (fp32 [C x HW], the NCHW slab) and a per-row bias b2' = W2*gb + b2 through EPILOGUE_BIAS, strided batch over images (B = 2..32, N = 49 / 196 / 784): time it against channels-last GEMM2 plus a 32x32 transpose-add kernel at 8,768, 8,384, 1,192; adopt swap-AB where it is <= channels-last + 3 us, else keep the transpose-add (5 launches on those rows). (c) A 4-launch stub (each kernel one dependent L2 round of the real bytes) to record the launch floor on this host. STEP 1, K1: 1-D cp.async.bulk plane copies into zero-padded smem (plane groups 16-B aligned; per-lane copies rounded outward to 16 B for 49-float planes; bank-skew slots for odd HW), one thread per 7-output row segment, 49 taps and bias in registers, per-token (sum, sumsq) partials; grid = (image, row strip) x cluster of 8 CTAs along channels (C/8 channels each: 96 at C=768, 48 at C=384, 24 at C=192, 20 at C=160); exchange the 2 floats per token through DSMEM (cluster barrier, each CTA reads the 7 peers' partials), then apply LayerNorm with lnw/lnb in-CTA and write a16 token-major [M][C] fp16 (or the channel-major TT layout if cuBLASLt's heuristic prefers it; test both at 8,768). Role CTAs (or a first round over all CTAs, all loads issued before use) convert W1 and W2 to fp16 with 16-B loads/stores, compute b2' in fp32 (hi/lo fp16 columns not needed since the bias is applied in fp32 by the epilogue), and issue cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2 of the fp32 W1/W2 at entry so the conversion reads hit L2 (I26). Also build a no-cluster control of K1 (d16 + stats, no LN) to isolate the cluster cost; report both. STEP 2, G1 per step 0a. STEP 3, K3': grid = B x (4C/KS) CTAs with KS = 256 (128 at C<=192), each reads its HW x KS fp16 slice (all tokens of its image) from L2 with every load issued first, column sumsq -> gf[k] = sqrt, red.add of its sum_k gf into a per-image fp32 cell plus a red.release arrival counter in a torch.empty int32 workspace with a generation word (self-resetting: the last arriver clears the cell and bumps the generation; correct for every call and shape order), spins with ld.acquire until the image's 4C/KS CTAs have arrived, computes s_b[k] = 1 + gw[k]*gf[k]/(mean + eps), rescales its slice in place (fp16) and adds gb[k] where the gb term is not folded into b2' (fold it: h' = h*s_b, bias b2' = W2*gb + b2). Co-residency: check with cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor that the grid fits in one wave (max 32x12 = 384 CTAs at 32,768) else launch cooperatively. STEP 4, G2 per step 0b. STEP 5, precision log, mandatory: fp64 reference, 10 seeded rounds from seed 200 with the harness generators, per row max |err| and the count beyond that row's own atol + 1e-5|ref|, for every path you ship (a16 is one fp16 rounding of a ~N(0,1) value, hidden one rounding, W1/W2 one rounding each). STEP 6, run_tests 16/16 with the portal-order check, interleaved with the r0 anchor; report per row rented time and launch count, and the step 0 probe numbers. Report what was not done. Success: Four launches on the wide-C rows (five if the transpose-add stays) and rented times at least 8 us under A r5 (8,768 48.1; 8,384 50.2; 16,384 62.1; 16,768 56.1; 32,768 70.2; 2,768 54.5) on three or more of the six rows, with 0 beyond-own-atol elements over the 10 seeded rounds on every shipped row; stretch: 1,192 <= 28, 4,192 <= 32, 8,192 <= 44 rented. Refuted if: The cuBLASLt GELU_BIAS epilogue costs > 3 us over BIAS at both 8,768 and 8,384 shapes (then the library epilogue route is dead and the finding goes to the pool), or the full four-launch pipeline is within 3 us of A r5 on all six wide-C rows in the same container. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): (1) The K3' arrival counter and generation word must NOT live in torch.empty memory: it is uninitialised and can hold any earlier tensor's bytes (tests pass by luck, the portal deadlocks). Put them in a module-level __device__ buffer zero-initialised at load, sized for the largest grid, and have the last arriver reset it, so every call and every shape order starts from zero. (2) cuBLASLt plans are shape-keyed, but the bias / epilogue pointers stored on a matmul descriptor (CUBLASLT_MATMUL_DESC_BIAS_POINTER etc.) change every call: set them on every call, never reuse a pointer from an earlier call. (3) cuBLASLt's GELU epilogue may be the tanh approximation of GELU: allowed only if the step 5 precision log is clean on every row that uses it; the tightest current row (1,96) already sits at 90% of its atol with the fp16 path, so log every shipped row.

Experiment E2 (tests H33): D: stamp the 2x at 32,768 / 14x14 rows, then cta_group::2 pairs or B multicast to lift the operand-ingest bound of the swap-AB tcgen05 engine. STEP 0: run_tests r4-d-tc05-swapab and the r0 anchor interleaved x3 in this container to set the session baseline (cross-host drift is 5-12 us). Deliver the owed precision log: fp64 reference, 10 seeded rounds from seed 200 with the harness generators, per row max |err| and beyond-own-atol count, for the r4 paths on the six wide-C rows and for the r3-ws-coop-widec path at 2,768 (the merge ships it). STEP 1: globaltimer stamps (CTA medians and max) at phase A end, sync 1, GEMM1 mainloop end, GEMM1 epilogue end, sync 2, GEMM2 mainloop end, red end, at 32,768, 16,384, 8,384 and 8,768; identify which term carries the ~2x above the 40-50 us bytes-and-ingest estimate (suspects: GEMM1 epilogue issue rate, doubled GEMM2 B ingest from g, scalar red volume, 2 tiles per CTA). STEP 2, ingest probe on the r4 gate GEMM (128xNT swap-AB tile, SW128 TMA ring, warm L2, clk per 64-k stage, N = 112 / 128 / 224, K = 768 and 3072, 148 CTAs): (a) 1SM as r4; (b) cta_group::2 pair: cluster 2x1, M = 256 across the pair (each CTA its 128 rows of the weight tile), each CTA loads half of the B token tile into its own smem, the even CTA issues the MMA with the pair descriptors, tcgen05.commit with the multicast form to both CTAs' barriers, consumer release through the cluster-scope barrier; (c) 1SM with the B tile TMA-multicast across a cluster of two CTAs that hold different weight tiles. Report clk per stage vs the MMA ideal (2N clk) for each; go with the variant at <= 1.3x the ideal; also record which of (b) and (c) wins, because that tells whether the H31 cap is SM-side or L2-side. STEP 3: port the winner into GEMM1 and GEMM2 of the cooperative kernel, keeping the cooperative launch, the validated descriptors (MN-major SW128 B: LBO 8192, SBO 1024; +2048 per k16), the bulk-plane conv and the CTA-local statistics; pair tiles must keep tile counts a multiple of 74 pairs per row (pick N and split-K per row). Fix the largest stamped term from step 1 (epilogue: 2 rows x 16 columns per lane with every tcgen05.ld issued first; red: red.global.add.v4 instead of scalar; B ingest: per-K-row s_b transform on the B stage instead of the g accumulator if the doubled ingest is the term). STEP 4: run_tests 16/16 with the portal-order check, interleaved with the parent and the r0 anchor; report per row rented times, the stamps before and after, and the per-stage clk. Reminder: target_hardware [B200] only; a release arrive from a warp with loads in flight stalls (tricks s5); clusters are allowed here because the GEMM tile needs them. Success: Per-64-k stage <= 1.3x the MMA ideal in the probe, and the full kernel at least 8 us under A r5 on three or more of 8,768 (48.1), 16,768 (56.1), 32,768 (70.2), 8,384 (50.2), 16,384 (62.1), with 2,768 <= 32 kept and 0 beyond-own-atol elements over 10 seeded rounds on the six rows. Refuted if: Both the pair and the multicast variant stay above 1.5x the MMA ideal per stage (then the ingest cap is not operand-bytes-per-SM and a wide-C single-launch design must reuse weight tiles from smem across all tokens instead), or the ported kernel is not >= 8 us faster than A r5 on any of the five rows. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds.
